## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of Linux privilege management, safe sudoers edits, and rollback procedures in a multi-tenant environment.

## Key Concepts
- Sudoers and drop-in files in `/etc/sudoers.d`
- User/group membership and least-privilege access
- `visudo` for syntax checking; rollback strategies
- Safe testing of privileges without exposing broad rights

## Code Example
```bash
id user; groups user
sudo -l -U user
cp /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.bak
printf 'user ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:/usr/bin/systemctl restart myservice\n' > /etc/sudoers.d/user
visudo -cf /etc/sudoers.d/user
sudo -n /usr/bin/systemctl restart myservice
```

```bash
# Show current governor

# Create a cpuset for tenantA
mkdir -p /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuset/tenantA

echo 0 > /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuset/tenantA/cpuset.mems

# Move tenant processes to the cpuset
pgrep -f tenantA | xargs -I {} echo {} > /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuset/tenantA/tasks

# Pin a process to specific CPUs
taskset -cp 0-3 <pid>
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical knowledge of diagnosing and mitigating network receive-path bottlenecks in a multi-tenant Linux environment, combining NIC hardware features, BPF-based flow steering, and per-tenant resource isolation with cgroups.

## Key Concepts

- **NIC RSS/XPS tuning**: Configure receive side scaling (RSS) and transmit packet steering (XPS) to hash tenant flows across multiple queues, avoiding single-core bottlenecks
- **Per-tenant CPU pinning**: Use cpuset cgroups to bind tenant-specific listener processes to dedicated CPU cores, preventing cross-tenant resource contention
- **Resource quotas**: Leverage cgroups v2 to enforce CPU and memory limits per tenant, ensuring fair resource allocation
- **Flow steering with tc clsact and eBPF**: Deploy eBPF classifiers in the qdisc to redirect packets to appropriate queues based on tenant metadata
- **Observability**: Monitor per-tenant latency tails, packet drops, and IRQ/CPU affinity to detect imbalances
- **Rollback and safe testing**: Implement automated rollback triggers based on latency and drop thresholds during load testing

## Code Example

```bash
# Create per-tenant cpusets
mkdir -p /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-a
mkdir -p /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-b

# Pin tenant processes to dedicated cores
echo 0-3 > /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-a/cpuset.cpus
echo 4-7 > /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-b/cpuset.cpus

# Set CPU and memory limits
echo 200000 > /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-a/cpu.max
echo 1G > /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-a/memory.max
```
